title: CMT-4 Security for ChaCha20-Poly1305-PSIV
summary: The HtE transform converts CMT-1 to CMT-4 but requires a suitable hash function; whether ChaCha20-Poly1305-PSIV can achieve CMT-4 security using only additional ChaCha20 permutation calls remains open.

formal_statement.body: $\mathrm{CMT\text{-}4}$ is a stronger security notion than $\mathrm{CMT\text{-}1}$: it replaces the requirement $K \neq K'$ with the weaker requirement $(K,N,A,M) \neq (K',N',A',M')$. Although the $\mathrm{HtE}$ transform converts a $\mathrm{CMT\text{-}1}$ scheme into a $\mathrm{CMT\text{-}4}$ scheme, it requires a suitable hash function. Determine whether ChaCha20-Poly1305-PSIV can achieve $\mathrm{CMT\text{-}4}$ security using only additional calls to the ChaCha20 permutation.

scope.domain: Authenticated-encryption and key-commitment security in ChaCha20-based symmetric cryptography.
parameters: Additional ChaCha20 permutation calls: permitted construction resource
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether ChaCha20-Poly1305-PSIV can achieve CMT-4 security using only additional calls to the ChaCha20 permutation.

progress.summary: The source contrasts CMT-4 with CMT-1 and notes that the HtE transform converts the latter to the former only with a suitable hash function. It explicitly leaves the ChaCha20-only construction question as future work.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., A Robust Variant of ChaCha20-Poly1305
